recipes.projection: Blended projection = weighted mean of Sleeper app x1, CBS Sports x1, ESPN fantasy x1, DraftKings points converted from each source's own stat lines. Weights renormalise over the sources that cover each player; coverage is the covering weight as a share of the total enabled weight. Coverage under 50% keeps the number from the sources that do cover the player and is flagged "thin"; it is never pulled toward a typical score for the salary. No coverage leaves the projection blank, flagged "no projection", unless the injury report lists the player as out, on IR, doubtful or suspended, in which case the projection is 0.
recipes.ownership: Own% is the average, by source weight, of the numbers Weekly findings file, Footballguys percent rostered and RotoWire projected roster % published for the DraftKings main slate; numbers for any other site or slate are never used. Stokastic DK cheat sheet is downloaded, stored and shown in its own column, but never averaged into Own% (weight 0). A number Adam types into the Own% cell replaces the published one for that player. A player with no published number is left blank: the app never estimates ownership, so game popularity exists only where a real number does.
recipes.scoring: DraftKings scoring from stat lines; 100/300-yard bonuses paid as 3 x probability from a lognormal (cv rush 0.55, rec 0.55, pass 0.30); DST points-allowed from a normal around the opponent's implied total (SD 9.5, shutout rate unvalidated)

injury.comment: Gibbs carried the ball 22 times for 153 yards and two touchdowns while catching seven of eight targets for 99 yards in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Patriots.
injury.longComment: Drake Maye (ankle) got knocked out of the game early for New England, setting the stage for the rout, and Gibbs took full advantage as he set new season highs in receiving yards and scrimmage yards. It's the fourth time in 2026 that the star RB has topped 150 rushing yards, and his fourth game with multiple TDs. Gibbs has amassed 1,384 scrimmage yards and 13 total touchdowns through nine contests as he gets ready to face a stingy Buccaneers run defense in Week 11.

injury.comment: questionable
Lamb secured seven of 13 targets for 72 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys' 46-40 loss to the 49ers on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Despite his own impressive numbers, Lamb played second fiddle to George Pickens for a change, as the latter doubled up the former in receptions and did the same with a yard to spare in receiving yards. Nevertheless, Lamb still put together a solid performance that included his eighth touchdown reception of the season, a spectacular leaping one-handed one-yard grab late in the fourth quarter. Lamb now is up to five consecutive double-digit target tallies and has at least 70 receiving yards in four of the last five contests heading into a Week 11 home matchup against the vulnerable Titans defense.

injury.comment: St. Brown caught four of five targets for 98 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Patriots in Munich.
injury.longComment: The Lions didn't need to throw it much, as Drake Maye (ankle) got knocked out of the game for the Patriots early. St. Brown took full advantage of the volume he saw however, scoring on a 56-yard catch and run in the first quarter and then taking another short pass from Jared Goff and turning it into a 28-yard TD in the third. It was St. Brown's third multi-TD game of the season but his first since Week 2, and he'll take a 65-755-7 line on 91 targets through nine games into a Week 11 clash with the Buccaneers.

injury.comment: Cook rushed 18 times for 157 yards and a touchdown and didn't catch his only target in Sunday's 31-12 win over the Jets.
injury.longComment: Buffalo relied primarily on its ground game in the lopsided victory, as Cook's 74-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter provided the cherry on top after a pair of one-yard Josh Allen rushing scores helped the Bills pull away. Cook extended his touchdown streak to eight games by scoring his ninth rushing TD over that span. He has topped 100 scrimmage yards in all but one game during the productive stretch, bouncing back effectively after being held to 69 scoreless yards by the Texans in the season opener. Cook has a nice opportunity to keep rolling in Week 11, when the 8-1 Bills host the 1-8 Dolphins.

injury.comment: Allen completed 11 of 21 passes for 196 yards, one touchdown and one interception while rushing five times for five yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 31-12 win over the Jets.
injury.longComment: Allen scored one-yard rushing touchdowns in the first and third quarters, bringing his season total up to 11 rushing TDs. He added his 13th touchdown pass of the campaign on a 45-yard strike to DJ Moore later in the third quarter, and Allen's fourth-quarter interception on third-and-long was basically an arm punt. Heading into a Week 11 home game against the Dolphins, the star QB has accounted for multiple touchdowns in all but one outing this season.

injury.comment: Hubbard carried the ball 27 times for 92 yards and two touchdowns and caught all five of his targets for 80 yards in Sunday's 20-17 win over the Saints.
injury.longComment: The 27-year-old RB kept the Panthers' offense afloat nearly single-handedly, as he set a new career high with 172 scrimmage yards while scoring both the team's TDs, on a two-yard run in the first quarter and a one-yard plunge in the fourth. Hubbard's 80 receiving yards were easily a new career high, topping the 3-57-0 line on three targets he recorded in Week 15 of the 2022 season against the Steelers. Over Hubbard's last six games, he surged to 697 scrimmage yards and six rushing touchdowns, and he'll look keep rolling in a Week 11 clash with the Ravens.

injury.comment: Flowers brought in six of seven targets for 74 yards and lost a fumble in the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday night.
injury.longComment: After being held to just three catches for six yards over the previous two games while Joe Fagnano primarily led the Ravens offense, Flowers got a major reprieve in the form of the debuting Jacoby Brissett. The talented wideout took advantage by finishing second in receptions and receiving yards for Baltimore on the night, but Flowers had the ball stripped from him after a 15-yard catch at the Chargers' 46-yard line with 2:11 remaining. The lost fumble turned out to effectively snuff out the Ravens' chances of realistically getting into position for a potential game-tying field goal, ending the game on a sour note. Nevertheless, the fact Brissett threw for 340 yards in his first game in the offense bodes well for Flowers' prospects as a Week 11 road matchup against the Panthers on Sunday approaches.

injury.comment: Williams rushed 16 times for 63 yards and brought in his only target for four yards in the Cowboys' 46-40 loss to the 49ers on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Williams had a near monopoly on the Cowboys' running back touches, but he worked hard for everything he got against a talented 49ers front seven. The veteran back averaged under 4.0 yards per carry for the seventh time this season, but he did eclipse 60 rushing yards for the third time in the last four games. Williams will take 692 rushing yards and nine rush TDs -- along with a 25-131-1 receiving line -- into a Week 11 home matchup against the Titans next Sunday.

injury.comment: Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak confirmed Monday that Bowers (ankle) is considered day-to-day after exiting Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports. "It's not as bad as we thought, but still a significant injury," Kubiak said.
injury.longComment: Bowers checked in and out of Sunday's contest as he managed the ankle issue, finishing with two catches for 18 yards on two targets while logging just 11 snaps on offense. Per Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com, Kubiak added that Bowers will continue to be evaluated throughout the week as the Raiders look to determine whether the star tight end will be available for next Sunday's game in Denver. If Bowers is forced to miss his third game of the season, the Raiders would have more targets up for grabs for the likes of tight end Michael Mayer, running back Ashton Jeanty and wideouts Tre Tucker, Jalen Nailor and Jack Bech.

injury.comment: Olave caught three of four targets for 30 yards in Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Panthers.
injury.longComment: The game wound up being Jordyn Tyson's breakout performance, as the rookie WR hauled in 11 of 13 targets for 80 yards, but that didn't leave much volume for Olave or any other Saint. With Tyler Shough struggling, it's unclear whether the passing game can keep more than one pass catcher fantasy-relevant at a time. Olave sports a 59-774-2 line on 87 targets through nine games, and he'll look to bounce back in a Week 11 tilt against the Bears.

injury.comment: Nabers secured five of seven targets for 44 yards and lost a fumble in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday.
injury.longComment: The star wideout finished with less than 50 receiving yards for the second time in five days, and Nabers' late third-quarter lost fumble had significant ramifications. The turnover came at the Commanders' 16-yard line with the Giants down by three, costing  New York a golden opportunity to tie the game at minimum. Nabers' aforementioned pair of mediocre performances have come in the wake of a four-game streak of 100-yard efforts in Weeks 4-7, and he'll look to boost his numbers back up against the Jaguars' pass-funnel defense in a Week 11 home matchup on Sunday, Nov. 22.

injury.comment: Head coach Todd Bowles said Monday that the Buccaneers "will try and lessen the load" on Irving following their Week 10 bye, Rick Stroud of the Tampa Bay Times reports.
injury.longComment: Though he hasn't shown any signs of wearing down while he's averaged a healthy 4.9 yards per tote through the Buccaneers' first nine games, Irving has already amassed 167 carries -- fourth-most in the NFL -- and would be on pace for a career-high 315 over the course of a 17-game schedule. Given the success they've found on the ground in recent weeks, the Buccaneers could continue to embrace a run-first attack, but expect Irving to cede a bit more work to backups Kenny Gainwell and Sean Tucker as Tampa Bay aims to keep their top back healthy for the long haul.

injury.comment: Swift rushed 12 times for 31 yards and didn't catch his lone target in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Buccaneers.
injury.longComment: Swift was bottled up by an elite Buccaneers run defense that came into Week 9 allowing a league-low 80 rushing yards per game. He nearly had a fumble in the fourth quarter but was ruled down by contact on a play that the Buccaneers unsuccessfully challenged. Swift's momentum came to an abrupt halt with this season-worst performance, as he failed to reach 70 scrimmage yards for the first time all season after racking up seven touchdowns in the preceding four games. After Chicago's Week 10 bye, Swift could be back to sharing the backfield with Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe), who hasn't played since Week 4 but recently returned to practice.

injury.comment: McMillan caught three of seven targets for 35 yards in Sunday's 20-17 win over New Orleans.
injury.longComment: The seven targets led the Panthers on the afternoon, but the second-year wideout wasn't able to do much with them. The 35 yards were McMillan's lowest total since Week 3, and he'll take a 49-660-3 line on 78 targets through nine games into a Week 11 tilt against the Ravens.

injury.comment: Tuten carried the ball 26 times for 88 yards and a touchdown and caught three of four targets for 25 yards in Sunday's 40-23 win over Tennessee.
injury.longComment: It's the second time this season that Tuten has reached triple-digit scrimmage yards in a game, with both those performances coming since the Jaguars' Week 7 bye. The second-year RB capped the rout with a six-yard TD run in the fourth quarter, extending his scoring streak to four games -- a stretch in which Tuten has racked up 260 rushing yards and three touchdowns on the ground while adding a 9-128-3 line on 10 targets through the air. He'll look to keep rolling in Week 11 against the Giants.

injury.comment: Pickens brought in 11 of 18 targets for 145 yards and three touchdowns in the Cowboys' 46-40 loss to the 49ers on Sunday.
injury.longComment: After watching fellow wideout CeeDee Lamb have several monster performances through the first half of the season, Pickens stepped up and took his turn in his return from a one-game absence due to a hamstring injury. Pickens was peppered with targets from Dak Prescott all afternoon, and the star receiver finished with career-high reception and target totals and a season high in receiving yards. Pickens struck from 35, 39 and five yards out on his trio of scoring grabs, which constituted Dak Prescott's first three TD passes on the day. A now clearly healthy Pickens is up to a 50-678-5 line on 80 targets for the season heading into a Week 11 home matchup against the Titans next Sunday.

injury.comment: Prescott completed 30 of 51 passes for 343 yards with five touchdowns and one interception while rushing four times for seven yards in the Cowboys' 46-40 loss to the 49ers on Sunday. He also ran for a two-point conversion.
injury.longComment: Playing catch-up from the second quarter on did wonders for Prescott's fantasy production, as the veteran quarterback sent 38 total targets in the direction of the talented trio of George Pickens, CeeDee Lamb and Ryan Flournoy alone. Prescott connected with Pickens for three of his scoring strikes, which went for 35, 39 and five yards. Flournoy (11 yards) and Lamb (one yard) accounted for the final two in the fourth quarter, and Prescott added a two-point conversion run after the final scoring toss with an admirable diving attempt on which he made contact with the pylon with the extended ball. Prescott tied a career high with his TD pass total, while his passing yardage was a season high. He should have an opportunity to put together a successful encore next Sunday, as a Week 11 home matchup with the vulnerable Titans secondary awaits.

injury.comment: Henry rushed 10 times for 10 yards and two touchdowns and brought in all five targets for 10 yards in the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday night.
injury.longComment: Henry was surprisingly stymied by a Chargers defense that had surrendered 4.9 yards per carry on the road coming in. The Ravens also threw an atypically high 49 times in Jacoby Brissett's team debut, leaving Henry with season lows in carries and rushing yards. However, the bruising back salvaged his night with his ninth and 10th rushing touchdowns of the season, which came from two and one yard out, respectively. Henry now has failed to eclipse 58 rushing yards in five consecutive games, but with Brissett significantly reviving Baltimore's air attack in his first start, better days should be ahead for the former in short order, beginning with Sunday's Week 11 road matchup against the Panthers.

injury.comment: Washington caught seven of nine targets for 152 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans.
injury.longComment: The 152 receiving yards were a new career high for Washington, and the fourth-year WR highlighted his big day with a two-yard TD toss from Trevor Lawrence in the first quarter to open the scoring. It's Washington's second game this season with 100-plus yards, and he'll take a 36-645-6 line on 64 targets through nine contests into a Week 11 tilt against the Giants.

injury.comment: Lawrence completed 25 of 35 passes for 352 yards and three touchdowns with one interception in Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans. He added 27 yards on four carries.
injury.longComment: It was another huge performance from the 27-year-old QB, as Lawrence set a new season high in passing yards and threw at least three TDs for the fifth time in nine games to begin the year. He spread the ball around again, as seven different Jaguars caught multiple passes and Parker Washington, Josh Cameron and Brenton Strange were all on the other end of scores. Lawrence will take a sharp 21:5 TD:INT into a Week 11 clash with the Giants.

injury.comment: Warren rushed seven times for 15 yards and brought in five of six targets for 26 yards in the Steelers' 38-18 loss to the Bengals on Sunday night. He committed a fumble recovered by Pittsburgh.
injury.longComment: The Steelers were quickly dissuaded from a balanced offensive approach when the Bengals accumulated 24 first-half points, leading to Warren's lowest carry and rushing yardage totals of the season. Warren did tie his second-highest reception total of the campaign thanks in part to how the game unfolded, but it was ultimately a nearly irrelevant fantasy night relative to the lofty standards the versatile back has set this season. Warren will look to get back on track at the expense of the struggling Eagles in a Week 11 intrastate road showdown next Sunday.

injury.comment: McBride tallied five catches on as many targets for 37 yards during Sunday's 34-6 loss to the Rams.
injury.longComment: McBride's streak of at least seven catches ended at 11 games, and his receiving yardage total marked his second-fewest of the campaign in what doubled as rookie QB Carson Beck's first NFL start. Better days likely are ahead for the duo, but as McBride works with his third signal-caller this season -- and the least experienced one at that after Jacoby Brissett and Gardner Minshew -- there may be more lows than highs for the tight end over the final seven contests. McBride will look to bounce back next Sunday at Kansas City.

injury.comment: Mahomes completed 22 of 35 passes for 348 yards with five touchdowns and no interceptions while adding two rushes for 15 yards in the Chiefs' 35-13 win over the Falcons on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Taking advantage of a controlled environment and a fast track at Mercedes-Benz Stadium -- not to mention the presence of the debuting Josh Downs -- Mahomes repeatedly exploited the vulnerabilities of the Falcons defense throughout the afternoon. The legendary signal-caller showed no ill effects from the elbow injury that he'd suffered in Week 9, and he connected with Emmett Johnson (12, six yards), Downs (18 yards), Cyrus Allen (39 yards) and Andrew Armstrong (43 yards) for his quintet of touchdown passes. Mahomes now has multiple scoring strikes and zero interceptions in three straight games, and Sunday's five TD tosses represented a new season high. Mahomes will take 2,385 passing yards and a 19:4 TD:INT into a Week 11 home matchup against the Cardinals next Sunday.

injury.comment: Pollard carried the ball nine times for 33 yards and caught eight of nine targets for 66 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 40-23 loss to the Jaguars.
injury.longComment: The veteran RB fell one yard short of reaching 100 scrimmage yards for a third straight game, and Pollard gave the Titans a brief glimmer of hope in the fourth quarter when he took a checkdown from Cam Ward 32 yards to the house, making the score 30-23. Pollard led the Titans in receptions as he produced season-best numbers through the air, and he could retain elevated usage as a pass catcher if top WRs Carnell Tate (shoulder) and Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) miss additional time. Pollard lines up for a potential revenge game in Week 11 against the Cowboys.

injury.comment: questionable
Wilson (concussion) caught seven of 14 targets for 106 yards and lost a fumble in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills.
injury.longComment: Wilson set a new season high in targets and came one yard short of his Week 3 season high Sunday in his return from a one-game absence due to a concussion. His production came on a mix of passes from Geno Smith (ankle) and rookie Cade Klubnik, the latter of whom saw his first NFL action after Smith exited in the second half. Wilson figures to work as the top target for whomever starts under center in a Week 11 road game against the Chargers.

injury.comment: Williams completed 22 of 37 passes for 279 yards, two touchdowns and four interceptions in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Buccaneers. He also rushed five times for 16 yards.
injury.longComment: Williams looked unstoppable early, capping Chicago's two first-quarter drives with touchdown passes of nine yards to Rome Odunze and 56 yards to Luther Burden, the latter of whom later exited due to a concussion. The 2024 first overall pick cooled down after that, throwing three second-quarter interceptions en route to a career-worst four interceptions overall. Chicago's defense picked up the slack with a pick-six against Baker Mayfield, and Williams found Colston Loveland for a 38-yard gain to set up Cairo Santos' game-winning field goal on the game's final play. The Bears have reeled off four consecutive wins since Williams returned from a hamstring injury to improve to 7-2, and he didn't have a turnover in the previous three games prior to Sunday night's downturn. Williams will look to clean up the errors in Week 11 against the Saints following Chicago's Week 10 bye.

injury.comment: Coleman carried the ball 17 times for 57 yards and a touchdown and caught all four of his targets for 31 yards in Sunday's 26-21 win over the Panthers.
injury.longComment: The rookie has seized control of the lead-back role for the Broncos, with his 21 touches dwarfing J.K. Dobbins' five, and Coleman's nine-yard TD run early in the fourth quarter put his team in the lead for good. Coleman has piled up 261 scrimmage yards and two rushing touchdowns over the last three games, and there's no reason to think his role will shrink on the other side of a Week 10 bye.

injury.comment: Bears head coach Ben Johnson confirmed Tuesday that Burden has cleared concussion protocol, Patrick Finley of the Chicago Sun-Times reports.
injury.longComment: Burden's status was up in the air for a bit with the Bears going on bye immediately after he sustained a concussion in a Week 9 win over the  Buccaneers, but he was spotted working out on the field with teammates Monday and has apparently cleared all five phases of the protocol. The second-year wideout looks like he'll be a full practice participant throughout Week 11, and he shouldn't face any playing-time limitations in Sunday's game versus the Saints.

injury.comment: Goff completed 20 of 31 passes for 303 yards and three touchdowns with two interceptions in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Patriots in Munich. He added three yards on his only carry.
injury.longComment: A potential barn burner versus Drake Maye never materialized when the New England quarterback left the game early with an ankle injury, but Goff and the Detroit offense still held up their end of the bargain. Two of Goff's TDs went to Amon-Ra St. Brown, including a 56-yard catch-and-run score in the first quarter, while Isaac TeSlaa also hauled in a 12-yard score in the second. Goff will take an 18:4 TD:INT through nine games into a Week 11 clash at home against the Buccaneers.

injury.comment: Barkley rushed 13 times for 22 yards and a touchdown while failing to catch his only target in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants.
injury.longComment: Barkley has mustered a meager 2.0 yards per carry over the past two games while playing through hamstring and back injuries, but he also has both of Philadelphia's touchdowns over that span, including a three-yard rushing score in the second quarter Sunday. It has been a slog offensively for the Eagles, who have tried first Tanner McKee and now Joe Milton under center since losing starting QB Jalen Hurts (IR, calf) likely for the season while also playing without top two wide receivers DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle). It's fair to wonder if Barkley will eventually be shut down as well to get a chance to heal as the 2-7 Eagles drop out of contention, but at least a Week 10 bye will offer him a respite before Philadelphia's Week 11 home game against the Steelers.

injury.comment: Rice brought in five of six targets for 82 yards in the Chiefs' 35-13 win over the Falcons on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Rice led the Chiefs in receiving yards and finished second in receptions and targets on a prolific afternoon for the Chiefs' air attack. Rice didn't get in on the scoring fun of a five-touchdown day for Patrick Mahomes, but he still eclipsed 80 receiving yards for the third time this season and first time since Week 3. Rice's level of involvement was encouraging given the debuting Josh Downs drew five targets, keeping the former's prospects bright for a favorable Week 11 home matchup against the Cardinals next Sunday.

injury.comment: Johnson rushed 22 times for 101 yards and brought in six of seven targets for 70 yards and two touchdowns in the Chiefs' 35-13 win over the Falcons on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Drawing his first career start due to Kenneth Walker (groin) being sidelined, Johnson put on a pretty convincing impression of his star teammate. Not only did Johnson just get himself over the century mark in rushing yards, but he finished as the team leader in receptions and targets while checking in as the runner-up in receiving yards. Johnson struck from 12 and six yards out for his two receiving TDs, underscoring his considerable versatility. If Walker is unable to garner active status for next Sunday's Week 11 matchup against the Cardinals, the Chiefs' ground attack will remain in good hands with Johnson.

injury.comment: Moore caught four of six targets for 90 yards and a touchdown while rushing once for four yards in Sunday's 31-12 win over the Jets.
injury.longComment: Moore's 45-yard touchdown catch in the third quarter accounted for half of his team-high total in receiving yards. This was his most productive outing since Moore went for 100 yards and a TD in his Bills debut, and the veteran wide receiver has chipped in 216 scrimmage yards and two touchdowns in three games since returning from a shoulder injury. Josh Allen and James Cook continue to lead Buffalo's offense with their legs, but Moore has re-established himself as Allen's top target in the passing game heading into a Week 11 home game against the Dolphins.

injury.comment: Hall rushed 11 times for 41 yards and caught all four of his targets for 67 yards in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills.
injury.longComment: Hall narrowly topped Braelon Allen (eight carries for 40 yards) for the team lead in rushing yards and finished second behind Garrett Wilson (seven catches for 106 yards) in both receptions and receiving yards. While Allen continues to be more efficient as a rusher, Hall's superior receiving ability should help the latter maintain the edge in playing time for a 2-8 Jets team that often finds itself playing catch-up. Rookie QB Cade Klubnik, who played most of the second half Sunday, could be more reliant on check downs to Hall than veteran Geno Smith (ankle) was, but it remains to be seen who will get the nod under center in Week 11 against the Chargers.

injury.comment: Williams caught four of seven targets for 50 yards in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Patriots in Munich.
injury.longComment: Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jahmyr Gibbs monopolized the Lions' offense on the day, scoring four of the team's five TDs, and there wasn't much production left over for Williams. The fifth-year wideout has topped 50 receiving yards just three times this season, and he'll take a 32-518-5 line on 51 targets through nine games into a Week 11 battle with the Buccaneers.

injury.comment: Shough completed 25 of 35 targets for 187 yards and one touchdown with one interception in Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Panthers. He added 25 rushing yards on six carries and was charged with a lost fumble.
injury.longComment: The second-year QB had more turnovers than TDs for only the second time this season, although his fumble may have been been more Audric Estime's fault, and Shough fell short of 200 passing yards for the third time. Rookie Jordyn Tyson was his top downfield option, catching 11 of 13 targets for 80 yards in a breakout performance, but no other Saint saw more than five targets or hauled in more than three passes. Shough will take a 15:7 TD:INT into a Week 11 clash with the Bears.

injury.comment: Skattebo rushed 18 times for 78 yards and two touchdowns and brought in three of four targets for 44 yards in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday.
injury.longComment: Skattebo put together an impressive all-around performance that included a season high in receiving yards. He also exceeded the 75-yard mark on the ground for the third time on the campaign, and he went in for his third and fourth rushing touchdowns of the season on one- and 13-yard runs in the first and third quarters, respectively. Skattebo didn't show any ill effects from the hamstring injury that cost him Sunday's win over the Eagles, and he'll now gear up for a Week 11 home matchup against the Jaguars' elite run defense on Sunday, Nov. 22.

injury.comment: Coker failed to catch any of his four targets in Sunday's 20-17 win over the Saints.
injury.longComment: While it looked like Coker was going to be in line for a breakout 2026 season after his 8-138-2 receiving performance in the Week 1 opener, Coker has been held to 23 catches for 255 yards and one touchdown over his last seven games. At this point, he can't be trusted in fantasy lineups until he shows something in the box score again. This was a pristine on-paper spot versus New Orleans in the dome, and next Sunday's home date against Baltimore won't be any easier.

injury.comment: Young completed 17 of 30 passes for 200 yards without a touchdown or interception in Sunday's 20-17 win over the Saints. He added one rushing yard on his only carry.
injury.longComment: Chuba Hubbard did most of the heavy lifting on offense for the Panthers, piling up 172 scrimmage yards and both the team's touchdowns. It's the first time this season Young failed to throw a TD, but it was also the first time since Week 6 he avoided committing a turnover. The fourth-year QB will take a 16:6 TD:INT through nine games into a Week 11 clash against the Ravens.

rows.name: Jaylen Waddle

injury.comment: Waddle (concussion) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Panthers, Parker Gabriel of The Denver Post reports.
injury.longComment: After being evaluated for a potential concussion, Waddle is done for the day and will thus target a potential return to action Nov. 22 against the Raiders, following Denver's Week 10 bye. In his absence Sunday, Courtland Sutton, Pat Bryant, Troy Franklin and Marvin Mims will handle the team's WR duties versus Carolina.

rows.prevGameWhy: the team's previous game on file is older than 11 days (likely a bye, or a game outside the main slate files)

injury.comment: Nix completed 25 of 37 passes for 237 yards and two touchdowns with one interception in Sunday's 26-21 win over the Panthers. He added two rushing yards on five carries.
injury.longComment: The Broncos had the home team right where they wanted them heading into the fourth quarter -- holding a lead -- and Nix worked his usual magic over the final 15 minutes, leading back-to-back touchdown drives capped by a nine-yard TD run from Jonah Coleman and a 26-yard strike to Pat Bryant for what proved to be the winning score. Nix did throw his first INT since Week 3 in the win, but he heads into a Week 10 bye with Denver riding a five-game win streak that has taken it to the top of the AFC West.

injury.comment: Gordon rushed 20 times for 76 and brought in four of five targets for 39 yards in the Dolphins' 24-22 loss to the Colts on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Filling his customary workhorse role in Miami's ground attack, Gordon handled all but four of the Dolphins' running back carries while finishing with a team-high reception total. The second-year back eclipsed 75 rushing yards for the fourth time in six games in the process, and Gordon's catch and receiving yardage totals were also season highs. Gordon should remain in a high-volume role in a Week 11 road matchup against the Bills next Sunday.

injury.comment: Likely brought in nine of 11 targets for 127 yards and a touchdown and fumbled once but recovered in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday.
injury.longComment: Likely set the pace for the Giants across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets, and his figure in the middle category also was a career high. The veteran tight end now has five double-digit target tallies on the campaign, and Thursday's production, which included a 66-yard catch-and-run touchdown in the third quarter, pushed his season line to a robust 55-575-7 line across nine games. All three components already are career-high figures, affording Likely massive momentum heading into a Week 11 home showdown against the Jaguars on Sunday, Nov. 22.

injury.comment: Ward completed 28 of 39 passes for 231 yards and two touchdowns with one interception in Sunday's 40-23 loss to the Jaguars.
injury.longComment: The second-year QB kept his team in the game for three quarters, and Ward connected with Tony Pollard for a 32-yard catch-and-run TD on a checkdown in the fourth quarter that brought the Titans to within one score, only for the Jags to pull away late. Ward's production is slowly creeping up, and he's thrown for 535 yards over the last two games with a 4:1 TD:INT, 68.4 percent completion rate and 6.8 YPA, numbers which represent a big step up from the beginning of the season. He'll look to keep making progress in his development in Week 11 against a vulnerable Cowboys defense.

injury.comment: Jeanty turned his nine carries into just 18 yards and caught all four of his targets for 46 yards during Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks.
injury.longComment: After reaching the 10-carry threshold in each of the first six games of the season, Jeanty has failed to do so in four straight contests, and he also has fallen shy of 30 rushing yards in six consecutive outings. Rookie RB Mike Washington continued to split the backfield with Jeanty in Week 10, turning his nine touches into 27 yards from scrimmage. Considering recent trends, Jeanty is difficult to trust for consistent production without a boost in work.

injury.comment: Titans head coach Robert Saleh said Monday that he's hopeful that Tate (shoulder) will return to action in Week 11 versus the Cowboys, Jim Wyatt of the team's official site reports.
injury.longComment: Even with the benefit of a Week 9 bye, Tate still wound up being sidelined for a second straight game in Sunday's 40-23 loss to the Jaguars on account of the shoulder injury. Though Saleh is optimistic that the rookie wideout will be ready to go for the Titans' upcoming game in Dallas, Tate will first need to return to practice in some fashion to make that a reality. Tate remained a non-participant in practice throughout Week 10 prep.

injury.comment: Rodgers completed 15 of 29 passes for 143 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions and rushed two times for minus-1 yard during Sunday's 38-18 loss at Cincinnati.
injury.longComment: The Steelers sat at 33 total yards of offense after three quarters, so the vast majority of Rodgers' output occurred on the team's three fourth-quarter possessions, two of which ended in touchdown connections with WR DK Metcalf (22 yards) and TE Pat Freiermuth (27 yards). Through nine games this season, Rodgers has tossed multiple TDs on five occasions, but he's also been held to less than 200 yards through the air three times. Rodgers will seek better results next Sunday in Phildadelphia.

injury.comment: Monangai (toe/thumb) was seen wearing full pads for the Bears' unofficial practice Tuesday, Adam Jahns of AllCHGO.com reports.
injury.longComment: After their Week 10 bye, the Bears won't post their first Week 11 practice report until Wednesday, but Monangai may be trending toward being listed as a full participant. The second-year back was on the field for a second straight day Tuesday and didn't appear to be operating with any limitations while mixing into drills. Monangai had missed the Bears' previous five games due to turf toe and a right thumb injury, but he looks poised to return to action this Sunday against the Saints.

injury.comment: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said that Cooper (ankle) will undergo imaging Monday, Eric Allen of the team's official site reports.
injury.longComment: Cooper played just one snap before exiting Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills after injuring his right ankle. Notably, the rookie first-round pick tweaked the same ankle in the Jets' Week 1 win over the Titans and was diagnosed with a high-ankle sprain, which resulted in a stint on injured reserve. The Jets are hoping that Cooper avoided as significant of an injury this time around, though even if his imaging yields good news, he still could be hard-pressed to suit up next Sunday versus the Chargers.

injury.comment: Mayfield (foot) "seems to be trending" toward sitting out Sunday's game against the Lions, with Jalon Daniels likely to draw the Week 11 start, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
injury.longComment: Coming out of a Week 10 bye, the Buccaneers have yet to provide official word on the status of Mayfield, whom Rapoport relays sustained a foot strain late in a Nov. 8 loss to the Bears that had relegated him to a walking boot over the past week. Given that Mayfield has shown a willingness to playing through injuries in the past, the Buccaneers will likely wait and see how he progresses as the week rolls along before making a decision on his status for Sunday, but Daniels looks like the early favorite to direct the Tampa Bay offense in Detroit. Daniels previously made starts from Weeks 4 through 6 while Mayfield was sidelined for all three games due to a dislocated right thumb.

injury.comment: Etienne carried the ball eight times for 14 yards and caught three of five targets for 20 yards in Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Panthers.
injury.longComment: Seeing his first action since Week 3 after recovering from a hamstring strain, the former Jaguar led the Saints' backfield with 11 touches, ahead of Audric Estime's eight and Alvin Kamara's five. Etienne wasn't able to do much with the volume, however, while Kamara scored two short TDs. Etienne still appears to be the top option for the team at RB, but if Estime keeps taking short-yardage work and Kamara is the preferred red-zone back, it would put a real ceiling on Etienne's upside. He'll look to claim a bigger share of the workload in Week 11 against the Bears.

injury.comment: Metcalf brought in two of six targets for 54 yards and a touchdown and added a two-point conversion catch in the Steelers' 38-18 loss to the Bengals on Sunday night.
injury.longComment: Metcalf's yardage total, modest as it was, led the Steelers on the night. The veteran receiver got there with the help of a team-long 32-yard catch, while his other reception was a 22-yard scoring grab early in the fourth quarter that Metcalf followed up with a two-point conversion. Metcalf has at least Sunday night's yardage total in three of the last four games, but he's still sporting an inefficient 35-432-2 line on 70 targets through nine games heading into a Week 11 road matchup against the Eagles next Sunday.

injury.comment: Flournoy tallied six catches for 71 yards and one touchdown on seven targets during Sunday's loss to San Francisco. He also recovered a fumble.
injury.longComment: Dallas played catch-up for much of the second half in the offensive slugfest, so quarterback Dak Prescott took to the air 51 times. Flournoy got seven of those targets, finishing third on the team behind George Pickens (18) and CeeDee Lamb (13). Flournoy's six receptions and 71 yards were both his second-highest figures so far this season, and the TD was his third in the past five weeks. That last stat in particular gives him relevance in most fantasy leagues, especially in matchups during which Prescott is expected to air it out often. The Cowboys will seek a much-needed win next Sunday at home against Tennessee.

injury.comment: Brissett completed 33 of 49 passes for 340 yards with no touchdowns and one interception and added two rushes for two yards in the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday night.
injury.longComment: Brissett looked like a natural fit in coordinator Declan Doyle's offense despite having only practiced a handful of days with the Ravens following his trade from the Cardinals, amassing his highest passing yardage total since Week 11 of last season. As he'd often done with Trey McBride in Arizona, Brissett focused heavily on the tight-end position in his Baltimore debut, connecting with Mark Andrews and Josh Cuevas a combined 11 times for 119 yards. Brissett recorded completions to seven different targets overall, but his one interception did lead to a Chargers touchdown. Brissett's prospects in this offense look bright if his first game is any indication, and he'll look to carry over the momentum into a Week 11 road matchup against the Panthers on Sunday.

injury.comment: Hampton rushed 22 times for 105 yards and a touchdown and brought in one of two targets for no gain in the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday night. He also fumbled once but recovered.
injury.longComment: On the momentous occasion of the Chargers' long-awaited first win of the season, Hampton made a significant contribution with a season-high rushing yardage total. The performance also marked the first time Hampton eclipsed the century mark this season, and he added his fourth rushing touchdown of 2026 on a one-yard power run on fourth down on the first play following the two-minute warning in the first half. Hampton now is up to 474 rushing yards and a 12-63-0 receiving line heading into a Week 11 home matchup against the Jets on Sunday.

injury.comment: Tyson caught 11 of 13 targets for 80 yards in Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Panthers.
injury.longComment: That bang you just heard was the sound of the window closing on your chances of acquiring Tyson cheaply in your fantasy league. In just his second career NFL game, Tyson dominated looks from Tyler Shough, as no other New Orleans pass catcher handled more than five targets, hauled in more than three passes or topped 30 receiving yards. It may be tough for the team's struggling offense to keep both Tyson and Chris Olave busy at the same time, so the duo may end up trading big games rather than opening things up for each other, but this kind of volume can't be ignored. Tyson will look for his first career touchdown in a Week 11 tilt against the Bears.

injury.comment: Egbuka (foot) caught three of five targets for 38 yards and added a one-yard run in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Bears.
injury.longComment: Egbuka returned from a two-game absence during which he was in concussion protocol in addition to dealing with a foot injury. He tied for second on the team in targets behind Cade Otton's eight and finished third in receiving yards behind Tez Johnson (76) and Kenny Gainwell (60), as Baker Mayfield spread the ball around to complement Bucky Irving's two-touchdown effort on the ground. Egbuka hasn't exceeded 63 yards in seven appearances this season heading into Tampa Bay's Week 10 bye.

injury.comment: Herbert completed 12 of 18 passes for 129 yards with no touchdowns or interceptions and rushed seven times for 51 yards and a touchdown in the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday night.
injury.longComment: Herbert ironically compiled his second-fewest passing yards of the season in the Chargers' first victory, but the talented signal-caller leaned heavily on both his legs and an effective rushing performance from Omarion Hampton. Herbert made a significant contribution himself to cap off Los Angeles' opening drive of the game, taking off when he couldn't find anyone open and recording a 22-yard rushing touchdown for the first points of the night. The game also marked Herbert's first interception-free performance of the season and gives the beleaguered Chargers' air attack something to hang its collective hat on heading into a favorable Week 11 home matchup against the Jets on Sunday.

injury.comment: Kamra rushed two times for four yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Panthers. He added three catches for 10 yards and an additional touchdown on four targets.
injury.longComment: With Travis Etienne back from his weeks-long hamstring injury that saw him miss five games while on injured reserve, the Saints deployed a three-man backfield committee against Carolina. Kamara scored a couple touchdowns, but it was a fluky performance on just five touches and 16 offensive snaps. Audric Estime logged 27 snaps and handled eight touches, while Etienne played 21 snaps and touched the ball 11 times. This is a backfield to avoid in fantasy while it the trio cancels each other out and caps each others' upside.

injury.comment: Dowdle rushed five times for 26 yards and caught both of his targets for eight yards during Sunday's 38-18 defeat at Cincinnati.
injury.longComment: Dowdle's previous low-water mark in touches was nine in Week 2 at New England, and on the season he averaged 11.8 touches per game entering Week 10 action. As a result, he finished with his second-fewest yards from scrimmage (34) in a contest this season, while backfield mate Jaylen Warren (12 touches for 41 total yards) also found little success in any facet. Dowdle remains the No. 2 RB in Pittsburgh behind Warren and thus is a hit-or-miss option in a Week 11 road matchup with the Eagles next Sunday.

injury.comment: Shakir caught two of three targets for 26 yards in Sunday's 31-12 win over the Jets.
injury.longComment: With Buffalo controlling this one most of the afternoon, Josh Allen attempted just 21 passes and completed only 11 on a day wind gusts played a factor. Shakir's 26 receiving yards were his fewest since Week 3. He's scored just one touchdown this season and has yet to hit 100 yards in a game all year, so the ceiling isn't that high for fantasy while the floor is what he produced Sunday. Shakir is more of fantasy WR4 in PPR-based formats.

injury.comment: Downs secured four of five targets for 53 yards and a touchdown, fumbled once but recovered and returned three punts for 10 yards in the Chiefs' 35-13 win over the Falcons on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Making his Chiefs debut following three days of practice after arriving via trade from the Colts on Tuesday, Downs looked right at home in the Patrick Mahomes-led offense. The young wideout fully capitalized on the upgrade he saw at quarterback, finishing third in receptions, receiving yards and targets right out of the gate and adding his second touchdown of the season on a difficult 18-yard catch just before halftime. Downs' immediate chemistry with Mahomes is highly welcome news for fantasy managers, and he'll aim to carry the momentum over into a favorable Week 11 home matchup against the Cardinals next Sunday.

injury.comment: Loveland caught four of six targets for 54 yards in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Buccaneers.
injury.longComment: Loveland was quiet for most of the night but got free for a 38-yard catch in the final minute to set up Cairo Santos' game-winning 38-yard field goal on the game's final play. The 2025 first-round pick has recorded at least 54 receiving yards in five of the past six games, having bounced back from a slow start to his sophomore season during which Loveland compiled just 34 yards through three games. Loveland will try to keep building momentum in Week 11 against the Saints following Chicago's Week 10 bye.

injury.comment: Mendoza completed 17 of 29 passes for 143 yards, no touchdowns and no interceptions and rushed six times for 22 yards and one TD during Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks.
injury.longComment: The Mendoza era in Las Vegas officially kicked off this week following the trade of veteran QB Kirk Cousins to the Vikings, and the rookie first overall pick unsurprisingly flashed at times while also stalling numerous drives by taking six sacks overall. On a positive note, Mendoza didn't turn the ball over, and he also recorded his first touchdown as a pro on a 10-yard run on the Raiders' opening offensive possession. He'll seek to build on the initial start of his career next Sunday at Denver.

injury.comment: Gainwell rushed five times for 16 yards and caught all three of his targets for 60 yards in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Bears.
injury.longComment: Most of Gainwell's 76 scrimmage yards came on a 44-yard catch. He has 304 scrimmage yards over the past three games after recording just 122 scrimmage yards across his first six outings for the Buccaneers. Bucky Irving rushed for two touchdowns Sunday and remains the top option in Tampa Bay's backfield, but Gainwell has started to make the most of his change-of-pace role in the Buccaneers' run-heavy offense. Gainwell will try to pick up where he left off in Week 11 against the Lions after a Week 10 bye.

injury.comment: Washington compiled eight rushes for 23 yards and secured his only target for four yards during Sunday's 21-13 defeat to the Seahawks.
injury.longComment: Aside from a 25-carry outburst in Week 8 at the Jets, Washington has logged 54 rushes along with four catches in nine appearances, which amounts to 6.4 touches per game. Despite that number, he continues to eat into the overall backfield picture, as lead runner Ashton Jeanty failed to tally double-digit rushes for a fourth straight contest Sunday. Washington should retain a modest role alongside Jeanty next Sunday at Denver.

injury.comment: questionable
The Titans placed Robinson (ankle) on injured reserve Tuesday, Jim Wyatt of the team's official site reports.
injury.longComment: Tennessee hasn't provided word on the severity of the ankle injury that Robinson sustained in the second half of this past Sunday's 40-23 loss to the Jaguars, but his move to IR ensures that he'll be sidelined for at least the next four games. While Robinson is out, Elic Ayomanor and Chimere Dike should be locked into top-three roles at receiver alongside rookie first-round pick Carnell Tate (shoulder), who has missed the past two contests but is expected back for a Week 11 matchup with Dallas. The Titans signed Xavier Restrepo off the practice squad to replace Robinson on the 53-man roster and bolster their depth at receiver.

injury.comment: Smith underwent tests Monday that didn't reveal a major injury to his left ankle, and he'll continue to be evaluated during the week before the Jets decide on his status for Sunday's game against the Chargers, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
injury.longComment: After exiting in the second quarter of Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills to get checked for a concussion, Smith returned to the contest in the third quarter but then left the game for good after sustaining an ankle injury. Fortunately for Smith, he appears to have avoided a significant injury, but he'll still need to prove his health during Week 11 prep in order to play Sunday. Head coach Aaron Glenn said Monday that Smith will remain the team's starter if healthy, but rookie Cade Klubnik would be in line to direct the offense against the Chargers in the event Smith can't play.

injury.comment: Johnson caught his only target for four yards in a 31-12 win over the Jets on Sunday.
injury.longComment: For the third time in seven appearances this season, Johnson didn't log a single carry. The veteran running back also didn't have much of a role in the passing game with just one target. In fact, Johnson tallied just 10 offensive snaps, finishing behind both starter James Cook (35) and fellow backup Ray Davis (12). Johnson has had a few productive performances as a pass catcher this season, but his role is too unpredictable to warrant weekly fantasy consideration.

injury.comment: Allen rushed eight times for 40 yards and caught his only target for six yards in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills.
injury.longComment: For a second consecutive game, Allen was outplayed by Breece Hall, who produced 108 scrimmage yards on 15 touches. Allen remains the more efficient runner, averaging 5.0 yards per carry to Hall's 3.4 this season, but Hall is the team's preferred option in passing situations, which have been plentiful with the 2-8 Jets frequently in catch-up mode. Perhaps a Week 11 matchup with a Chargers team that's still searching for its first win through Sunday of Week 10 will offer an opportunity to stick with the run and play to Allen's strengths.

injury.comment: Allgeier mustered five carries for 14 yards and didn't gather in his only target during Sunday's 34-6 defeat to the Rams.
injury.longComment: With Bam Knight back in the lineup in Week 10 after one absence due to a concussion, Allgeier didn't reach double-digit touches for the first time since Week 5, a span in which the latter's 65 touches went for 334 yards from scrimmage and two total TDs. Knight himself found a similar lack of success Sunday with just 19 yards on his five rushes. Because the Cardinals racked up just 123 yards of offense in rookie QB Carson Beck's first NFL start, it's tough to envision worse outcomes moving forward, though the team does take on the surging Chiefs next Sunday on the road.

injury.comment: Mitchell caught three passes for 59 yards on eight targets in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills.
injury.longComment: With Garrett Wilson back from his one-game absence Sunday, Mitchell was left fighting for secondary looks. His eight targets were second on the team, trailing Wilson's 14, and Omar Cooper's early-game ankle injury helped Mitchell's volume solidify. If Cooper is going to miss time going forward, Mitchell will be a more comfortable fantasy WR3 play with upside headed into next Sunday's game against the Chargers.

injury.comment: Washington secured all three targets for 50 yards, threw a 34-yard touchdown on his one pass attempt and returned four punts for 36 yards in the Dolphins' 24-22 loss to the Colts on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Washington finished second in receiving yards for the Dolphins and also was partly responsible for the team's one score through the air, uncorking a well-thrown 34-yard strike to Jalen Tolbert on a trick play. Washington also continued to produce in his returner role, and he's now up to 812 all-purpose yards through nine games heading into a Week 11 road matchup against the Bills next Sunday.

injury.comment: McCarthy completed 23 of 36 passes for 293 yards with a touchdown and an interception while adding six rushes for 34 yards in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday.
injury.longComment: McCarthy continued to look like a competent NFL signal-caller in his third start for the Giants, posting a new career high in passing yards and adding a new season high in rushing yardage. His one touchdown pass was a critical one, as he hit Isaiah Likely over the middle for a 66-yard score just before the midway point of the fourth quarter to erase a 17-14 deficit. McCarthy has displayed excellent chemistry with his top targets, and he'll look to keep his hot streak going against a pass-funnel Jaguars defense in a Week 11 home matchup on Sunday, Nov. 22.

injury.comment: Singletary played just five snaps on offense and took one carry for three yards in Thursday's 24-21 loss to the Commanders.
injury.longComment: Cam Skattebo came back from a hamstring injury and dominated backfield work, taking 21 touches for 122 yards and two touchdowns on an 88 percent snap share. Singletary played 92 percent of snaps the week before in a win at Philadelphia, but his 23 touches went for just 39 total yards and no TDs. It'll likely be another large workload for Skattebo when the Giants host the Jaguars in Week 11.

injury.comment: Rodriguez rushed for five yards on four carries in Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans.
injury.longComment: Rodriguez was out-carried 26 to four by Bhayshul Tuten, who has very much proven himself as the Jaguars' clear RB1 in one of the league's best offenses. Tuten also out-snapped Rodriguez 52 to 10, while LeQuint Allen (12 snaps) saw more playing time. Rodriguez is little more than a deep-league bench stash should something happen to Tuten.

injury.comment: Tucker caught one pass for nine yards on two targets in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks.
injury.longComment: In Fernando Mendoza's first career start at quarterback, Tucker saw just 6.9 percent of the targets, while Jack Bech led the team with seven looks. Tucker looks like someone who won't be usable in fantasy until he shows some tangible chemistry with the young quarterback.

injury.comment: Bernard failed to reel in any of his three targets while notching a 10-yard rush during Sunday night's 38-18 loss to the Bengals.
injury.longComment: Bernard went without a catch for the first time since Week 1, and his three targets were his fewest since the team's Week 4 loss to the Browns. The wide receiver led his position in offensive snaps (58), besting DK Metcalf (50) in that regard. Bernard entered Week 10 having recorded multiple receptions in five straight contests, and he'll have a good shot to get back on track in Week 11 versus the Eagles.

injury.comment: Kincaid caught two of three targets for 58 yards in Sunday's 31-12 win over the Jets.
injury.longComment: Kincaid contributed catches of four and 54 yards to finish second on the team in receiving yards behind DJ Moore (90). The 2023 first-round pick has seen his usage fluctuate throughout the campaign, as Kincaid has failed to exceed three targets on five occasions but has drawn at least six looks from Josh Allen in each of the other four games. Kincaid is making the most of his opportunities for a second consecutive regular season, averaging 11.9 yards per target in 2026 after leading all qualified TEs with 11.7 YPT in 2025. Next up for Kincaid is a Week 11 home game against the Dolphins.

injury.comment: Milton completed 18 of 34 passes for 169 yards, no touchdowns and no interceptions in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants. He also rushed nine times for 64 yards, ran in a two-point conversion and lost a fumble.
injury.longComment: The big-armed Milton wasn't effective as a passer while working with a depleted receiving corps that was missing DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), but Milton showcased strong mobility and led the Eagles in rushing yards while RBs Saquon Barkley and Elijah Mitchell combined for just 28 rushing yards on 16 carries. The 2024 sixth-round pick of the Patriots played nearly the full game in the 2024 regular-season finale against the Bills and got into four games with Dallas during the 2025 campaign, but this was Milton's first regular-season NFL start. Philadelphia's Week 10 bye will provide an opportunity to evaluate a QB room consisting of Milton, the recently benched Tanner McKee and rookie fifth-round pick Cole Payton. Whichever QB gets the starting nod in Week 11 against the Steelers would benefit from the potential return of Smith or Wicks after the bye.

injury.comment: Hill turned three carries into four yards and added five catches on seven targets for 34 yards during the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday.
injury.longComment: Hill also had a 14-yard carry midway through the first quarter, but the play was nullified by an offensive holding call. The veteran running back connected on a 17-yard catch with Jacoby Brissett late in the third, which set up a 36-yard field goal by Riley Patterson four plays later. Hill's five catches were a season high, and even with the Ravens' quarterback carousel over the last three weeks, the 2019 fourth-rounder has hauled in at least three passes in each of his last five outings. Losers of five straight games, the Ravens will look to turn their fortunes around in a Week 11 road tilt against the Panthers on Sunday.

injury.comment: Vidal turned two carries into zero yards, brought in both of his targets for 14 yards and returned one kickoff for 32 yards during the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday.
injury.longComment: Vidal's 15 offensive snaps were just ahead of Keaton Mitchell's 13, but both running backs took a back seat to Omarion Hampton, who was on the field for 36 of the Chargers' 57 snaps on offense and led the backfield with 22 carries for 105 yards and one touchdown. Vidal's two carries were his fewest since Week 3 against the Bills (1), although his 15-yard catch early in the third quarter set the Chargers up just outside the red zone, with Cameron Dicker connecting on a 34-yard field goal four plays later. Vidal and Mitchell will continue to operate in rotational roles behind Hampton heading into Week 11 against the Jets on Sunday.

injury.comment: Sutton caught five of nine targets for 45 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-21 win over the Panthers.
injury.longComment: The five grabs and nine targets led the Broncos on the day, but Pat Bryant just edged him out for the receiving yards lead. The highlight of Sutton's solid performance was a three-yard TD from Bo Nix in the first quarter, as none of his receptions went for longer than 12 yards. Denver gets a well-timed bye in Week 10, but if Jaylen Waddle (concussion) isn't cleared to play on the other side of it, Sutton could see bigger volume in Week 11 against the Raiders. On the season, the long-time Bronco sports a 25-266-2 line on 46 targets through nine games.

injury.comment: Vele caught both of his targets for 14 yards during the Saints' 20-17 loss to the Panthers on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Vele was on the field for 55 of the Saints' 63 offensive snaps, which was second most among wide receivers behind Chris Olave (56). Despite that playing time, Vele saw only two targets Sunday, although no other Saints pass catcher logged more than three receptions other than rookie first-rounder Jordyn Tyson, who finished with 11 catches on 13 targets for 80 yards. Vele has two receptions in each of his last two outings, and it appears his role in the Saints' passing offense has shrunk due to the return of Tyson. Vele will look to bounce back for Week 11 against the Bears on Nov. 22, and Chicago's defense ranks 15th in the NFL in fantasy points allowed to receivers per game.

injury.comment: Kelce secured both targets for 30 yards in the Chiefs' 35-13 win over the Falcons on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Kelce recorded a 23-yard catch on the Chiefs' first play from scrimmage, seemingly a harbinger of a productive day. However, the veteran tight end also suffered an ankle injury on the tackle, and although he was able to return to the game, he had only one more reception the rest of the way. Despite the modest numbers, Kelce managed to keep his season-long streak of games with multiple receptions going, and he's averaging a career-best 14.6  per catch heading into a Week 11 home matchup against the Cardinals next Sunday.

injury.comment: Beck was 11-for-18 passing for 108 yards, no touchdowns and two interceptions and had one rush for one yard during Sunday's 34-6 loss to the Rams.
injury.longComment: The Cardinals traded Jacoby Brissett to the Ravens after Week 8, and then Gardner Minshew tore the UCL in his right elbow in Week 9, setting the stage for the first appearance (a start) of Beck's career. Beck, a rookie third-rounder, generated just two drives of 30-plus yards among his nine possessions overall, and two others ended in interceptions in Rams territory. He also didn't find much success with his top available skill-position talent, TE Trey McBride, who gathered in all five of his targets for 37 yards. They'll look to improve their rapport next Sunday in Kansas City.

injury.comment: Dobbins rushed four times for 18 yards and caught his only target for four yards during Sunday's 26-21 win over Carolina.
injury.longComment: Dobbins saw 13 fewer carries than rookie running back Jonah Coleman (17-57-1) in the game. The four rushes were a season low for Dobbins, and he figures to continue to operate as the team's No. 2 option in the backfield moving forward.

injury.comment: Abdomen
Odunze caught four of seven targets for 60 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Buccaneers.
injury.longComment: Odunze bobbled what should have been an easy touchdown catch and failed to get down inbounds by the time he secured the ball, but he made amends two plays later with his first touchdown catch of the season to cap Chicago's opening drive from nine yards out. He had another critical drop later in the game but still finished second on the team behind Luther Burden (concussion) in targets, catches and receiving yards. Burden exited late in the game, and if Chicago's Week 10 bye doesn't provide the team's leading receiver enough time to clear concussion protocol, Odunze could get an uptick in opportunities in Week 11 against the Saints.

injury.comment: Lemon caught six of nine targets for 61 yards in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants.
injury.longComment: Lemon showed a nice rapport with QB Joe Milton in Milton's first NFL start, as the rookie first-round pick led the Eagles in catches, receiving yards and targets. Lemon has operated as Philadelphia's de facto No. 1 WR while DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) have both missed the past three games, but the Eagles could get at least one of their top two wideouts back in Week 11 against the Steelers following a Week 10 bye.

injury.comment: Goedert caught five of six targets for 50 yards in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants.
injury.longComment: Goedert finished one catch and 11 yards shy of Makai Lemon's team-leading totals in Joe Milton's first start for the Eagles. Both of Goedert's touchdowns this season came back in Week 1, and the Eagles have since changed QBs twice. Goedert's best result in the three games started by Tanner McKee was a six-catch, 61-yard outing, so the veteran TE has remained consistent even as the offense around him falls apart due to injuries. Milton, McKee and rookie fifth-round pick Cole Payton are all potential candidates to start in Week 11 against the Steelers after Philadelphia's Week 10 bye.

injury.comment: McCord completed 17 of 32 passes for 209 yards with no touchdowns or interceptions and rushed twice for four yards and a touchdown in the Dolphins' 24-22 loss to the Colts on Sunday. He also lost a fumble that was returned for a touchdown.
injury.longComment: Drawing his first career start as a result of Malik Willis having gone on injured reserve with an abdomen injury earlier in the week, McCord acquitted himself well overall in a favorable matchup. The 2025 sixth-round pick of the Eagles spread the ball around to nine different targets, and he had a statement three-yard touchdown run on the first play of the fourth quarter when he powered through a pair of defenders and broke the plane despite having his facemask pulled. McCord's one turnover was very costly, however, as it was recovered on the Dolphins' six-yard line and returned for a short touchdown. McCord should only get more comfortable by following up Sunday's solid showing with another week of practice, but he'll draw a tough Week 11 road matchup against the Bills next Sunday.

injury.comment: Brooks (groin) has been downgraded from doubtful to out for Sunday's game against the Saints, Joe Person of The Athletic reports.
injury.longComment: Brooks ended Week 10 prep with back-to-back limited practices, but he was tagged as doubtful for Sunday's game against the Panthers. The third-year running back is not quite fully recovered from a groin injury that landed him on IR in late September, so his next chance to suit up is Week 11 against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 22. Trevor Etienne, AJ Dillon and Anthony Tyus will continue to operate in rotational backfield roles behind Chuba Hubbard while Brooks is sidelined.

injury.comment: Spears rushed four times for 28 yards in Sunday's 40-23 loss to the Jaguars. He turned one catch into zero yards on one target.
injury.longComment: After missing the previous two games with a knee injury, Spears returned to play 16 offensive snaps. Tony Pollard (41 snaps) remains the clear-cut lead back on this cellar-dwelling Tennessee team. Spears has minimal fantasy appeal now that Pollard survived the trade deadline and will finish out the season with the Titans.

injury.comment: Vaki turned six carries into 28 yards and added a 17-yard catch on his only target during the Lions' 35-10 win over the Patriots on Sunday in Munich.
injury.longComment: Lead back Jahmyr Gibbs dominated with 252 yards and three touchdowns on 29 total touches (22 carries, seven catches on eight targets), but Vaki also had his moments during Sunday's game, including a 17-yard catch on the first play of the second quarter. Vaki was working through an ankle issue during Week 10 prep before being cleared to play, and he'll continue to operate in a rotational role in the backfield behind Gibbs. Through eight regular-season games, Vaki has turned 36 carries into 163 yards (4.5 YPC) and eight catches on nine targets for 81 yards. The Lions will be at home for three of their next four games, starting with Week 11 against the Buccaneers on Nov. 22.

injury.comment: Johnston brought in his sole target for six yards in the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday night.
injury.longComment: The speedster was poised to see some added involvement with Ladd McConkey (back) sidelined, but that never materialized on a night when 86 of Justin Herbert's 129 passing yards went to Tre' Harris. Johnston's yardage total was a season-low figure, and he's now been limited to one reception in four of the last five games. Johnston's often been able to offset the modest catch totals with big plays, but that clearly wasn't the case Monday night. Johnston will remain a hit-or-miss fantasy option in a Week 11 home matchup against the Jets on Sunday, irrespective of McConkey's availability.

injury.comment: Meyers caught three of six targets for 34 yards in Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans.
injury.longComment: The six targets were second on the Jaguars behind Parker Washington's nine, but Meyers' longest gain of the day went for only 15 yards. The veteran wideout has also failed to find the end zone in six straight games, a stretch in which he's managed just a 19-256-0 line on 32 targets. Meyers will try to end that drought in a Week 11 clash against the Giants.

injury.comment: Klubnik completed 11 of 20 passes for 137 yards, no touchdowns and one interception in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills. He added three rushing attempts for 26 yards.
injury.longComment: Klubnik saw the first regular-season action of his NFL career in the second half of Sunday's loss, as Geno Smith (ankle) exited the game. The rookie fourth-round pick led the offense down to Buffalo's four-yard line on his first possession in the third quarter, but the Jets settled for a field goal on that possession, and Klubnik was picked off on his next drive. If Smith isn't ready to return in Week 11, Klubnik would be in line to make his first regular-season start on the road against the Chargers.

injury.comment: Davis rushed three times for eight yards in Sunday's 31-12 win over the Jets.
injury.longComment: Davis has been held to single-digit rushing yards in eight of nine games this season and has now managed to rush for just 52 empty yards on 16 carries for the season. He's nothing more than a bench stash in fantasy should something happen to James Cook.

injury.comment: Johnson recorded two tackles on special teams during the Bears' 27-24 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) was inactive for a fifth consecutive game, with Johnson operating as the Bears' RB2 behind D'Andre Swift in the Bears' four contests prior to Sunday against the Bucs. However, Johnson didn't play a single offensive snap against Tampa Bay; instead, it was Salvon Ahmed (five carries for 25 yards) who mixed into the backfield as Chicago's complementary piece to Swift. The Bears are on a bye for Week 10, with their next game taking place in Week 11 against the Lions on Sunday, Nov. 22. Johnson would have a narrow path to offensive relevancy if Monangai is cleared to return for that contest.

injury.comment: Knight turned five carries into 19 yards, failed to haul in either of his two targets and recorded a tackle during the Cardinals' 34-6 loss to the Rams on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Knight was cleared to return for Week 10 from a one-game absence while in the league's concussion protocol. His 19 snaps were actually ahead of fellow running back Tyler Allgeier (16), with the duo each logging five carries, although the Cardinals logged only 35 offensive snaps for the entire game and finished with a measly 17:37 time of possession. It was Arizona's first game with rookie third-rounder Carson Beck under center, and Knight and the offense will have its hands full in Week 11 against Kansas City, whose defense ranks eighth in the NFL in yards allowed per game (314.8).

injury.comment: Douglas brought in three of eight targets for 71 yards in the Dolphins' 24-22 loss to the Colts on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Douglas posted a team-high yardage total with a big hand from his game-long 38-yard grab. Douglas garnered plenty of first-time starter Kyle McCord's attention as evidenced by the receiver's team-high target tally, and he's now hit or exceeded the 70-yard mark in three of the past four games. The 2026 third-round pick will look to carry over the momentum into a tough Week 11 road matchup against the Bills next Sunday.

injury.comment: Coach Mike McCarthy said Monday that the Steelers are "hopeful" they can get Pittman -- who last played in Week 4 -- back from his foot injury this week, Nick Farabaugh of PennLive.com reports.
injury.longComment: The same goes for Roman Wilson (finger), who saw his last game action in Week 5. In the duo's absence, DK Metcalf has led Pittsburgh's WR corps, with Germie Bernard having seen his role expand in the process. Prior to his injury, Pittman caught seven of his 12 targets for 89 yards in three games, but once he rejoins the lineup, the 29-year-old -- who had at least 111 targets in each of his last five seasons with the Colts -- could resurface on the fantasy radar in PPR formats.

injury.comment: LaPorta caught one of four targets for 16 yards in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Patriots in Munch.
injury.longComment: The Lions didn't need to throw it much, as Drake Maye (ankle) got knocked out of the game for the Patriots early, and LaPorta simply didn't get many chances to make an impact. It was the worst performance of the season for the fourth-year tight end, but LaPorta's gone four straight games without reaching 40 receiving yards or getting into the end zone. He'll try to break out in Week 11 against the Buccaneers.

injury.comment: Daniels "seems to be trending" toward drawing the start at quarterback for the Buccaneers on Sunday in Detroit while Baker Mayfield tends to a foot strain, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
injury.longComment: Mayfield injured his foot late in a Week 9 loss to the Bears, and after he was in and out of a walking boot during the Buccaneers' Week 10 bye, his status is firmly up in the air for Week 11. Since Mayfield has shown a willingness to play at well below 100 percent in the past, the Buccaneers will likely wait until the end of the week to see where he stands on the health front before naming a starter for Sunday, but Daniels at least appears poised to take some reps with the first-team offense when the team returns to practice Wednesday. When Mayfield was previously sidelined from Weeks 4 through 6 due to a dislocated thumb, Daniels stepped in as the starter and guided Tampa Bay to a 1-2 record while completing 60 of 95 passes (63.2 percent) for 501 yards, three touchdowns and four interceptions to go with 117 yards on 19 carries.

injury.comment: Hamstring
Estime carried the ball seven times for six yards and caught his only target for five yards in Sunday's 20-17 loss to Carolina.
injury.longComment: Travis Etienne returned from IR and led the Saints' backfield with 11 touches, although he managed just 34 scrimmage yards, while Alvin Kamara handled five touches and scored two short TDs. Perhaps worse for Estime's role and future value, he was ineffective in short-yardage situations, getting stuffed on three attempts to pick up a first down from two yards out or less, and a miscommunication with Tyler Shough on a handoff led to a lost fumble in the second quarter, although the giveaway was charged to the QB. Estime will try to maintain some share of the workload in a Week 11 meeting with the Bears.

injury.comment: Coleman caught one of three targets for 11 yards during Sunday's 31-12 win over the Jets.
injury.longComment: Coleman failed to reel in multiple passes for the third time in the team's last five contests, and he played just 52 percent of the team's offensive snaps in the contest, his lowest percentage since Week 1. The wide receiver was briefly sidelined while being evaluated for a head injury before returning to the contest, which likely contributed to his lower workload. Coleman will continue to be an unpredictable fantasy option in Week 11 versus the Dolphins.

injury.comment: questionable
Mayer caught two of three targets for 16 yards in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks.
injury.longComment: Jack Bech (seven targets) was the only Las Vegas player to see more than four targets in Fernando Mendoza's first career start. The rookie quarterback targeted 10 different players on his 29 attempts. With Kirk Cousins' efficiency off to Minnesota, Mayer is a low-floor TE2 for fantasy, but he could get a bit of a boost if Brock Bowers' ankle injury causes him to miss time.

injury.comment: McKee (ribs) is active for Sunday's game against the Giants.
injury.longComment: McKee has overcome his rib injury in time to suit up for Sunday's contest. The quarterback is set to back up Joe Milton against the Giants due to the absence of former starter Jalen Hurts (calf, IR).

injury.comment: Updating a previous report, Conner (foot) no longer appears to be a candidate to return from injured reserve to play Week 11 versus the Chiefs, according to Tyler Drake of ArizonaSports.com.
injury.longComment: A report Monday from Jess Root of USA Today quoted Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur as stating that Conner was "trending well" and had "a chance" to return to action in Week 11, but Drake clarified that LaFleur was referring to guard/center Jon Gaines (ankle) rather than Conner. The veteran running back hasn't played since Week 3 of the 2025 season due to a right foot/ankle injury that required surgery, and he remains without a clear timeline to return to the field. Conner took part in individual drills during training camp, but after being placed on IR on Aug. 30, he hasn't been cleared to resume practicing since the regular season got underway.

injury.comment: Mitchell turned three carries into four yards, failed to haul in his lone target and returned two kickoffs for 30 yards during the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday.
injury.longComment: One of Mitchell's carries went for 11 yards, but his other two rushes went for minus-five and minus-two yards, and all of those touches came on the same drive in the second quarter. His 13 offensive snaps were third-most among Chargers running backs behind Kimani Vidal (15) and Omarion Hampton (36), and it was Hampton that commanded the majority of backfield touches, finishing with 22 carries for 105 yards and a touchdown.
